transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-18
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Ng (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (Aegis Health - ML Eng), Lisa Chen (Aegis - Product), Rajiv Menon (Aegis - Security)

Summary:
Weekly POC sync focused on quality evaluation results from last week's prompt sets, regression checks after model/config changes, and next steps for hardening guardrails. Customer highlighted a small regression in one funnel and security clarified KMS/audit expectations for Private if pilot moves forward.

Topics:
- Eval scorecards and failing prompt clusters
- Guardrail efficacy (toxicity/PHI redaction and routing)
- KV/prefix caching impact on score drift
- Dedicated pool benchmark to rule out perf-induced regressions
- Security/compliance checklist for Private deployment

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sophie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, is the audio ok?
[00:06] Michael (Aegis): Yep all good, thanks.
[00:10] Sophie: Cool. Today we wanted to walk through the quality evals from last week's runs, go over the regressions you flagged, and define next steps. Devon will lead on the diffs.
[00:20] Devon (Redwood SE): Yep, thanks. I pulled the eval sheet you shared, link in chat: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/aegis-pilot - I also attached the token-level diffs.
[00:30] Lisa (Aegis): We saw a drop in precision on the clinical-summarization prompts, around 4 points, and some hallucinations in the 'med history' examples.
[00:40] Devon: Right, so preliminary root cause looks like a combo of the quantized runner we flipped last week plus prefix caching that not always matching the prompt normalization. So two things: kernel path changes and caching mismatch can change the soft probabilities and that yields different top-k outputs.
[00:55] Michael: When you say prefix caching mismatch, can you spell that out? We were assuming cache would only help.
[01:00] Devon: Sure. The approximate behavior: when the prefix tokenizerization differs slightly - whitespace, tokens, or odd unicode - the KV cache hits are less likely and the model takes a cold path which changes sampling. We saw this with a set of 42 prompts in the "med-history" bucket. Some transcripts show kay-vee cache spelled out in logs, so apologies for bad automated transcribe, but that's what we meant.
[01:20] Sophie: Important detail: we also rolled a small quantization tweak (int8->q4_0) on the dedicated replica for cost testing. That can subtly change logits. We expected some delta but not this direction.
[01:30] Michael: Is this something you can revert for the pilot to see if scores recover?
[01:33] Devon: Yes, we can roll the q profile back and re-run overnight on the dedicated pool. We'll also re-run with caching on/off to isolate.
[01:40] Rajiv (Aegis - Security): Quick security question: if we move to Private or VPC, do you keep audit logs for model inferences e.g., request/response? We need retention and KMS integration for PHI.
[01:50] Sophie: Yes, in Private we can ship audit logs, and we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. I'll share the security pack.
[02:00] Rajiv: Great, please include retention windows and what fields are redacted by default.
[02:05] Sophie: Will do.
[02:08] Devon: Back to the evals — I ran the scoring using your rubric: relevance, hallucination rate, and redaction accuracy. The scoring script is in the sheet; note there's a small mismatch where the tokenizer in our scoring harness uses gpt-tokenizer v0.9 and the deployed runtime uses a slightly different tokenizer fallback in edge conditions, so some of the token-aligned metrics are off.
[02:30] Lisa: That's probably why we saw diffs in the entity redaction pass. Some PII still slipped through.
[02:35] Devon: Exactly. For reliability we recommend: 1) pin tokenizer and model variant in the config used by the eval harness; 2) run a token-level diff with and without cache; 3) add guardrail tests for the top 200 prompts as a regression suite.
[02:50] Michael: Can you show one of the failing examples?
[02:55] Devon: Yep, example ID AEG-2025-03-11-17: prompt was 'Summarize recent meds and list allergies' - baseline model returned 'No known allergies' incorrectly when the note included 'allergic to penicillin'. The probability mass shifted slightly such that the summarizer ignored the sentence fragment.
[03:20] Michael: That one is high severity for us. Any quick mitigations?
[03:24] Devon: We can add deterministic extraction fallback for critical fields (allergies/meds) — a rule-based extractor as guardrail before summarization — and hide that behind a confidence threshold. Also we can increase beam/search temp to push recall on entity extraction.
[03:40] Lisa: Adding a rule-based extractor is fine, but who maintains that? We want avoid ops burden.
[03:45] Sophie: Redwood can ship a maintained extractor as part of the pilot add-on, or we can provide the patterns and code for your team. We'll scope maintenance cost if you choose Redwood-managed.
[03:55] Rajiv: On encryption - if we keep logs, are response tokens stored in plaintext? That is a compliance red flag.
[04:02] Sophie: By default hosted logs are encrypted at rest; in Private you can use your KMS. We can also redact or hash PHI fields before persistence. We'll include the exact config options in the security doc.
[04:12] Michael: Good. Back to the technicals, do you think the regression is more due to quantization than caching?
[04:18] Devon: Early signs point 70/30 in favor of quantization. The q4 path changes logits more broadly. Cache mismatches exacerbate but are secondary. We'll confirm by rolling back q profile and comparing the metric deltas.
[04:30] Sophie: Next milestone: confirm if reverting q profile restores scores; if yes then we'll propose a q-profile that balances cost and quality for your workloads. Also we'll ship an updated guardrail set for the top failure classes.
[04:42] Lisa: For the evaluation cadence, we want weekly diffs but also a lightweight daily smoke check for critical prompts. Can you do daily smoke runs limited to 50 critical prompts?
[04:52] Devon: Yes that's doable through our scheduled eval runner. We'll set up a cron in the pilot account to run the 50-critical set and push alerts when precision drops below your threshold. Please confirm the exact thresholds.
[05:03] Michael: Target: precision >= 92% and recall >= 88% for allergies/meds buckets.
[05:08] Devon: Got it, we'll configure alerting.
[05:12] Sophie: Action recap - we'll re-run the failing set with q-profile toggled and cache toggled; update sheet; share security doc; and scope the extractor option. Any other blockers?
[05:22] Rajiv: One more: can you provide an SSO cert for test environment and list of roles for RBAC?
[05:26] Sophie: Yes, we'll send SAML metadata and RBAC matrix.
[05:30] Lisa: Also, pricing — if we need dedicated for runs, what is the delta for reserved vs burst?
[05:36] Sophie: I'll include detailed pricing scenarios in the follow-up email — reserved monthly commit vs on-demand bursts. Expect a delta in unit cost but more predictable latency on reserved.
[05:45] Michael: Sounds good.
[05:47] Devon: One more small note: some transcription artifacts in the logs spelled 'Redwood dedicat' etc, sorry, auto-transcribe typo in the artifact names.
[05:55] Sophie: No worries. We'll send everything in one package. Thanks everyone.

Closing recap and links:
- Eval spreadsheet: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/aegis-pilot (updated soon)
- Token-diff logs: https://redwood.app/logs/aegis-token-diffs/20250318
- Security pack (will be shared): https://redwood.app/security/aegis-pilot-pack.pdf

Explicit next steps (as discussed):
- Devon to run q-profile rollback tests and caching toggles, post results and token diffs by 2025-03-24.
- Sophie to update the eval spreadsheet with guardrail flags and pricing scenarios by 2025-03-20.
- Rajiv to provide compliance question list and confirm retention windows by 2025-03-21.
- Team to schedule dedicated cluster benchmark if regression persists (tentative 2025-03-25).

End of meeting.
